children: Oil futures fall in early Asian trade on possible position adjustments after rising overnight but near term losses are likely to be limited by ongoing Middle East tensions. Yemen's Houthi militants struck a building at the headquarters of Saudi Arabia's state oil giant in the eastern city of Dhahran, the WSJ reported, citing people familiar with the matter. "Hostilities intensified in the Middle East, threatening further supply disruptions," ANZ Research analysts say in a research report. Also, "attacks on oil tankers in the Persian Gulf continued unabated," they add. Front-month WTI crude oil futures are 0.6% lower at $94.54 per barrel; front-month Brent crude oil futures are 0.6% lower at $105.39 a barrel. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
